claim_boundary: In a zero-axiom Rocq development, a relative count that is natural, invariant under constant Weyl rescaling and satisfies the chain rule is multiplicative in the scale ratio, hence determined on dyadic scales by a single number; and that number is forced to one exactly when an absolute reference region is assumed to exist.

closes_gate.how: The refutation killed the ABSOLUTE count and asked what the DOF-independence assumption becomes. A RELATIVE count survives the same dilation argument, and is then pinned down completely: multiplicative, hence generated by a single number.

does_not_establish: that the exponent is positive, or that it equals a dimension. Monotonicity is NOT assumed, so the power-law reading is prose
the scaling law beyond dyadic scales. f(2^n) = f(2)^n is proved; extending to all rationals or reals needs a regularity argument not given here
that DOF-independence really becomes additivity of the exponent. That reading is stated, not proved: no product structure on regions is formalised
the geometric inputs from differential geometry. They are explicit hypotheses, as in the companion files
anything about curved configurations, non-constant conformal factors, or extra structure
any claim about general relativity or its dynamics
a reproduction, confirmation or refutation of Carcassi--Aidala's own derivation
any quantum, causal, or field-theoretic claim
gate_negative_controls: eleven inherited from the earlier modules, all rejected
a FALSE claim that the relative count is trivial WITHOUT the reference assumption is REJECTED -- so the relational notion is genuinely non-degenerate, not a second collapse

the_finding.derivation: With the chain rule nu(U,W) = nu(U,V) nu(V,W) and f(t) = nu(ball t, ball 1), chaining through ball b and using dilation invariance with c = b gives f(ab) = f(a) f(b). Hence f(2^n) = f(2)^n: the entire family is generated by one number.
the_finding.statement: What survives of 'how many degrees of freedom' in a conformally invariant theory is not a function on regions. It is a single scaling exponent.
the_finding.the_two_results_are_one: If some region could serve as an absolute reference -- if nu(-, ball 1) were itself dilation invariant, which is exactly what having an absolute count would mean -- then f(2) = 1 and the exponent collapses. The exponent is nonzero PRECISELY because no conformally invariant reference exists. The refutation and this certificate are the same fact from two sides.
the_finding.what_their_assumption_becomes: '#states = product of #confDOF' is a PRODUCT of counts. Products of ratios are sums of exponents, so DOF-independence survives as ADDITIVITY OF THE EXPONENT over independent subsystems, not as a product of counts. That reading is prose; only the scaling law is proved.

the_move.to: nu(U, V), degrees of freedom in U relative to V
the_move.why_it_survives: Dilation invariance now acts on BOTH arguments: nu(dil c U, dil c V) = nu(U, V). Applied to balls that says nu(B_r, B_s) depends only on the ratio r/s, which is not degenerate. It is the familiar content of conformal invariance -- there is no length, only ratios of lengths.

theorems.name: self_ratio_is_one
theorems.statement: a relative count is one at every region

theorems.name: ratio_sees_only_the_scale_ratio
theorems.role: the dilation argument does not kill a RELATIVE count -- it says exactly that absolute scale is meaningless while ratios of scale are not
theorems.statement: nu(ball (a c), ball (b c)) = nu(ball a, ball b)

theorems.name: scale_factor_is_multiplicative
theorems.statement: f(ab) = f(a) f(b) for f(t) = nu(ball t, ball 1)

theorems.name: generated_by_a_single_number
theorems.role: THE ANSWER. The whole family is generated by one number: what survives is a scaling exponent, not a function on regions.

theorems.name: a_reference_region_forces_a_trivial_exponent
theorems.role: the exponent is nonzero PRECISELY because no conformally invariant reference exists; this and the refutation are one phenomenon seen from two sides
theorems.statement: if nu(-, ball 1) were itself dilation invariant then f(2) = 1

theorems.name: trivial_exponent_makes_every_dyadic_scale_tie

theorems.statement: and then every dyadic scale ties
